fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. "When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet." (Proverbs 3:24). The writer is telling his son to preserve sound judgment and discernment, and this promise is part of what follows. No fear when you lie down, and sweet sleep when you rest. I'd sign up for that one TWICE.

Yes, friend. "He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble." (Proverbs 3:34). Grace goes to the humble. This verse is a pair, and the two halves pull in opposite directions. Mockers get mocked, the humble get grace, and I know which side of that pair I'd rather stand on.

Yes, friend. "The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame." (Proverbs 3:35). Honor goes in the first blank, and it's what the wise inherit. This is the closing line of the passage. Nice pairing, and it sets up the second blank perfectly.

Exile sounds like a big, dramatic ending for fools, friend, but this verse doesn't use that word. It says, "The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame." (Proverbs 3:35). Honor is what the wise inherit, and shame is what fools are held up to. Those two words side by side are your blanks.
